# `set_lock_position`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Set the guider lock position, either exactly or snapped to the star at that position.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build matches (READ)) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, guider handler @0x7a620 (64-bit build); Guider::SetLockPosition @0xe9370, SetLockPosToStarAtPosition @0xe9670 |

Params is an object {x, y, exact} or a positional array [x, y, exact]. x and y are required numbers (pixels, unchecked). With exact true the lock position is set to the given point; otherwise the guider selects the star at that position. The call is refused while the guider is calibrating or guiding.

Side effects: Changes the guide target (lock position) inside the guider. When reached through an imager relay on the main table the same request can additionally trigger the reconnect callback described in the guider service notes (relay eligibility is a separate outer gate).

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"set_lock_position"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | Object {x, y, exact} or positional array [x, y, exact]. x and y are pixel coordinates in the guide image with no bounds check in the handler. exact is optional. [READ] |

| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). ## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 108 | x or y missing or not a number | `expected float param` |
| 106 | exact present with a type other than boolean or integer | `expected bool param` |
| 300 | Internal failure (no guider object or star selection failed) | `internal error` |
| 304 | Guider is in the calibrating or guiding state (exposed states 2 or 3) | `could not set lock position when calibrate or guide` |
| 305 | Lock position could not be set (other refusal) | `could not set lock position` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request is not an object, is an empty object, or has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: no method of type string (a non-string method counts as missing) | `invalid request` |
| 101 | Dispatcher: text fails to parse | `invalid JSON request: <reason> on line <n> ...` |
| 103 | Dispatcher: unregistered method | `method not found` |

The exact trigger split between 300 and 305 is not established beyond the labels.

## Example

Request, request - Object form (shape READ; values invented):

```json
{"id":8,"method":"set_lock_position","params":{"x":640.5,"y":360.0,"exact":false}}
```

Request, array:

```json
{"id":9,"method":"set_lock_position","params":[512,300,true]}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_lock_position","result":0,"code":0,"id":8}
```

Reply, busy:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_lock_position","error":"could not set lock position when calibrate or guide","code":304,"id":10}
```
